candidates.summary: The set \(\WFF\) of well-formed formulas is the smallest set of strings satisfying the following formation rules: \begin{enumerate} \item Every propositional variable \(P\in\Prop\) belongs to \(\WFF\). \item If \(\varphi\in\WFF\), then \(\neg\varphi\in\WFF\). \item If \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\) and \(\circ\in\{\land,\lor,\to,\leftrightarrow\}\), then \((\varphi\circ\psi)\in\WFF\). \item No string is a well-formed formula unless it is obtained by finitely many applications of the previous clauses. \

Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). The set \(\Gamma\) is finitely satisfiable if every finite subset of \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable. \[ \operatorname{FinitelySatisfiableSet}(\Gamma) \Longleftrightarrow \forall\Delta\,\Bigl((\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\land \Delta\text{ is finite}) \Rightarrow \operatorname{SatisfiableSet}(\Delta)\Bigr). \]

A preorder $(I, \leq)$ is \emph{directed} (or a \emph{directed set}) if every finite subset of $I$ has an upper bound in $I$: for all $i, j \in I$ there exists $k \in I$ with $i \leq k$ and $j \leq k$.

Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). A subset \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\) is a finite unsatisfiability witness for \(\Gamma\) if \(\Delta\) is finite and unsatisfiable. \[ \operatorname{FiniteUnsatisfiabilityWitness}(\Delta,\Gamma) \Longleftrightarrow \Delta\subseteq\Gamma\land \Delta\text{ is finite}\land \operatorname{UnsatisfiableSet}(\Delta). \]
Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable, then every finite subset of \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable.
A \emph{term}, also called a \emph{conjunction term}, is a finite conjunction of literals.
A \emph{clause} is a finite disjunction of literals.

Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\) be a finite list of propositional variables. A \emph{maxterm} relative to \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\) is an \hyperref[def:elementary-disjunction-propositional-logic]{elementary disjunction} that contains exactly one of \(P_i\) or \(\neg P_i\) for each \(i=1,\ldots,n\).

candidates.summary: The depth of a formula \(\varphi\), denoted \(\operatorname{depth}(\varphi)\), is defined recursively: \begin{enumerate} \item if \(\varphi\) is atomic, then \(\operatorname{depth}(\varphi)=0\); \item if \(\varphi=\neg\psi\), then \(\operatorname{depth}(\varphi)=\operatorname{depth}(\psi)+1\); \item if \(\varphi=(\psi\circ\chi)\), then \[ \operatorname{depth}(\varphi)=\max\{\operatorname{depth}(\psi),\operatorname{depth}(\chi)\}+1. \] \end{enumerate}
